text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chairman of the Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, said in a speech a key to success of Bosnia's peace process is the removal of war criminals. Reconciliation and true peace can come only after war criminals are tried in the Hague, Izetbegovic said.

- Croat representatives on Monday refused to sign an amendment to agreement on joint police force in Mostar area. Disputed amendment requires national balance of future police force to be based on 1991 census.

- Commissioner of the International Police Task Force (IPTF), Manfred Seitner, says that IPTF will not participate in formation of joint police force unless the amendement is signed by both Croat and Moslem parties.

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic said on Monday that her dispute with the rest of the Serb leadership is not based on ideological but economic reasons. "When I touch grey economy, it is as if I stick a finger in their eye," Plavsic says.
- Former president of Bosnian Croat self-styled state of Herceg-Bosna, Mate Boban, died on Monday in Mostar after suffering a stroke.

- The NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia rejected a Serb media report about an alleged mobilisation of Moslem-Croat army. Major Chris Riley said SFOR supervises activities of the armies in both of Bosnia's entities and "there are no indications the federation army is preparing actions against the Serb entity."

- The Bosnian trade union filed a protest to the federation government regarding the latest announcement of a hike in prices for electricity, heating, rent, water, and postal services. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
